title: When plain objects/functions are simpler than classes
learningObjectives: Explain when plain objects/functions are simpler than classes and choose suitable object-oriented patterns.

understand.concept: Plain objects are effective for simple records, configuration, and data transfer. Functions are effective for focused behaviour. Classes are useful when many instances share behaviour and invariants. Choose based on the problem rather than using classes by default.
understand.whyItMatters: Overengineering small data structures adds indirection and maintenance cost. A simple object literal is often clearer than a class with no meaningful instance behaviour.
understand.analogy: Use a simple container when all you need is storage; build a specialised machine only when it provides a real capability.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript object identity, prototypes, and class semantics are defined by the language.

explain.narrative: The record needs no class hierarchy. A small function expresses the behaviour directly.

examples.explanation: The record needs no class hierarchy. A small function expresses the behaviour directly.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the object creation or class behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Take a plain data record and decide whether it needs a class. Explain what shared behaviour or invariant would justify introducing one.
practise.independentTask: Model a small domain using the simplest suitable object pattern. Explain the trade-offs between plain objects, functions, prototypes, and classes.
hints: Separate instance data from shared behaviour.
Check own properties and inherited properties.
Prefer composition when capabilities need to vary independently.

questions.prompt: When is a plain object often the better choice?
options: When the data is simple and has no meaningful shared instance behaviour
questions.answer: When the data is simple and has no meaningful shared instance behaviour
questions.explanation: Plain objects avoid unnecessary abstraction for straightforward data records.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between a plain object, function, and class?
options: The actual data and behaviour requirements
A rule that every object must be a class
The number of lines in the file name
questions.answer: The actual data and behaviour requirements
questions.explanation: Choose the least complex abstraction that clearly expresses the required behaviour.
